svg.title: One advisor question: the function-call loop of the Responses API
svg.desc: Sequence with four lifelines: Sami, the coordinator; Karim's advisor host in Python; the Foundry project's Responses API running agent cedar-dispatch-advisor version 3; and the deterministic ranker with the facts snapshot. Step 1: Sami asks who should take WO-1101. Step 2: the host creates a response with the conversation ID, the question and the agent reference. Step 3: the model plans and returns a function_call item rank_candidates with arguments work_order_number WO-1101 and call ID call_1; nothing in Foundry runs Cedar code, and the run expires after 10 minutes. Step 4: the host validates the argument and runs the ranker, which returns Riverstone Mechanical first with high acceptance, high on-time and heavy load, then AquaFlow Plumbing, bands only, no figures. Step 5: the host sends a function_call_output item for call_1 in the same conversation. Step 6: the model writes the answer from the tool output. Step 7: the host's guard checks GD-1 to GD-5: no figures, no action claims, only names from the tool output, rank 1 first, the no-eligible wording. If it passes, Sami sees the model's answer; if it fails, Sami sees the rules-only summary built from the same tool output.
svg.text: One question to the Dispatch Advisor: who runs what
model plans; Foundry runs no Cedar code;
1 Riverstone (high, high, heavy) · 2 AquaFlow (medium, low, light)
bands only: no rates, counts or scores
6 answer text from the tool output
from the tool · rank 1 first · no-eligible
pass: model answer · fail: rules-only summary
Identities: Foundry sees the question and the tool output; the host reads Cedar facts with its own identity; Sami needs no Azure role.
